default_avoid: text, letters, numbers, captions or signage that was not specified
logos, brand marks, watermarks or signatures
extra, missing or fused fingers, limbs or joints
duplicated people or objects, or a person merged into an object
shadows that disagree with the light direction, or a second sun
warped or bent straight lines in walls, tiles, frames or furniture
people or objects whose size does not match their distance
reflections that do not match what stands in front of the surface
tilted water lines, liquid that does not fall downward, fabric that ignores gravity

checks.question: Could every made object in the frame actually work: fastenings that fasten, straps and cords that go somewhere, strings and cables under the right tension, handles, hinges and controls where a hand could reach them?
Is every made object complete and symmetrical where its design is symmetrical, with no part fused into another and no edge that dissolves into a smudge?
Is everything held or worn held or worn the way it is actually used, rather than in a grip or a position that would not work?
Is the image free of text, numbers, signage, logos and watermarks the spec did not ask for, and free of lettering that reads as distorted or nonsensical glyphs?
Does every visible hand have five fingers, and every person the right number of arms, legs and joints, each bending the way a joint bends?
Are the proportions right: neck, arm and leg lengths, head size against body, with no limb stretched or shortened to fit the frame?

Do the eyes, teeth, ears and any eyeglasses hold up close: matching pupils and catchlights, a gaze that goes somewhere, teeth that are separate from the lip and gum, frames that rest on the ears and nose?
Does each person own their own body: no shared or merged limb between two people, no arm that belongs to nobody?
Does each hand that holds something close around it, with the fingers on the near side in front and the far side hidden?
Do both eyes point where the spec says, with an expression that fits the action rather than a blank or over-glossy stare?
Do skin, hair and fabric read as real material rather than wax, plastic or airbrush, with pores, stray hairs and creases where real ones would be?
Does the whole frame look like one photograph: the same sharpness, grain and noise throughout, with no element that looks cut from a different picture?
Does the scene look like something that happened rather than a staged shoot: no impossible tidiness, no everybody-in-focus-and-smiling perfection the brief did not ask for?
Does the image hold exactly the people and objects the spec names, with nothing duplicated, merged or added?
Do the shadows of every person and object run in the same direction, so that one light position explains all of them at once?
Do the shadow lengths match one light elevation, and does the line from each object to its own shadow point back toward the same light?
Does everything resting on a surface meet it, with a contact shadow in the gap, so that nothing floats and nothing sinks into the floor?
Is every object supported the way the spec says, and would it stay there under gravity rather than tipping, sliding or hanging from nothing?
Do the parallel planes in the frame agree: floor, counter, table and shelf edges converging on one horizon rather than each to its own?
Do all the figures stand on one floor, with their feet on a ground plane that recedes consistently, rather than on separate invisible shelves?
Does the horizon cross each standing person at the height the spec's camera height requires, the same share of their height for everyone of equal height?
Is every person and object the size its distance requires, measured against the scale anchors in the spec?
Does every nearer thing overlap the things behind it consistently, with no element both in front of and behind the same object?
Do the lines that are straight in the world stay straight and evenly spaced: wall edges, tile grids, window frames, stair treads, shelf fronts?
Does sharpness fall off with distance from the focus plane, with nothing behind a soft plane rendered sharper than it?
Does every mirror, glass and glossy surface show what actually stands in front of it, in the right place, and does transparent material bend what is behind it?
Do liquid surfaces sit level, pours fall downward, steam rise, and fabric hang and crease under gravity rather than floating or standing stiff?
Do the local details in the spec read correctly for the stated place: the script on signage, uniforms and dress, plates, plants, architecture, fittings?
Is the area the spec reserves for a headline or logo quiet enough to carry type at the published size?
Does the subject survive the crops the spec names, with nothing essential cut at the stated aspect ratios?
